device.name: Antelope Orion Studio III
device.notes: Composite USB device; control is entirely via the vendor HID interface (iface 3). UAC2 audio-control interface has no Feature Units.

command.notes: The general-purpose 'set one param for one target' frame. Used for every per-input-channel param (gain, mode, phantom, phase) AND for the new per-bus params (bus_level/bus_dim/bus_mute/bus_mono) -- see 'buses' below. channel_offset means different things depending on the param: a physical input index (0-11) for channel params, or a bus id (0/1/2/5) for bus params. No known GET/query opcode -- state is read passively from IN reports.

link_command.notes: A SEPARATE frame shape from the SET_PARAM command above -- do NOT build it with build_command()/build_raw_command(). param_id_offset (16) lines up with SET_PARAM's, but there is no per-channel byte at offset 17 (always 0/unused here); instead pair_index lives at offset 18 and an explicit enabled 0/1 lives at offset 19 (SET_PARAM has no equivalent of this second byte). Confirmed from capture chlink (2026-08): all 6 channel-link pairs toggled on then off in turn, and the pair_index/enabled bytes were read directly off the wire for every single command -- see params.channel_link.

state_report.notes: Parallel-array layout: all channel gains contiguous from gain_base_offset, all status bytes contiguous from status_base_offset. Formula: status_byte = (phase<<6)|(phantom<<4)|(mode&0x03).

bus_block.notes: Same 'parallel array, N bytes per slot' idea as gain_base_offset/status_base_offset above, but for output buses instead of input channels: byte offset for bus N = base_offset + bytes_per_bus*N + field_offset. Confirmed for bus ids 0, 1, 2, 5 (captures mona/hp1/hp2/monb, 2026-08) by ramping bus_level through its whole 0-96 range and toggling dim/mute/mono in isolation, and cross-checking every SET_PARAM command in the capture log against the very next state_report reading at this formula's offset for that bus id -- matched every time. reserved_byte_offset (+2) never changed in any of the 4 captures; true padding, or just never exercised, is unconfirmed. Bus ids 3 and 4 were never sent in any capture, so their slots (offsets 37-39 and 40-42) are unconfirmed -- see 'buses' below.

meter_report.channel_meter_scale: inverted: 0x60 (96) at rest/silence, falls toward 0x00 as input level rises
meter_report.notes: One byte per channel, same order as gain/status. Offset formula confirmed for all 12 physical channels (each channel's meter tracks its own signal correctly -- 2026-08). dB calibration (db_curve) comes from a channel-0-only sweep; applied to all channels for lack of a per-channel calibration, see db_curve_notes.
meter_report.db_curve_notes: Channel 0 only, 1kHz sine, gain swept down from max while phase_invert was clicked as a timestamp marker at each reference point (a real command, so it shows up as an unambiguous status-byte bit flip -- a cheap way to bookmark a capture without a second command-frame log). Raw byte == -dB, essentially exactly, across the whole 0 to -60dB range swept (the -60 point originally logged as raw=59, not 60, but that was the user eyeballing a color bar rather than a number while manually dragging the gain slider -- not curve non-linearity, corrected to 60). Not yet swept: the red/orange LED boundary, and anything past -60dB (one stray, unexplained data point -- raw=72 at gain driven to 0/deep silence -- doesn't fit this line at all, but wasn't a deliberate reference point, see notes above). Not yet confirmed on other channels, but likely identical given the same offset formula holds for all 12.

led_scale.notes: Confirmed 2026-08: no separate solid-red band below clip -- orange runs all the way to 0dB, red only appears at clip.

channels.notes: Formula (byte17=N, gain@49+N, status@61+N) confirmed for all 12 physical hybrid inputs via the CLI. Hi-Z is only offered on channels 1-4 (indices 0-3) on real hardware; hiz_channels reflects that hardware constraint (user-reported, not yet cross-checked against a capture of the Launcher graying out the option on ch5-12).

link_pairs.formula: pair_index = channel_index // 2 (0-indexed channels). pair 0 = ch1&ch2, pair 1 = ch3&ch4, pair 2 = ch5&ch6, pair 3 = ch7&ch8, pair 4 = ch9&ch10, pair 5 = ch11&ch12.
link_pairs.notes: See params.channel_link for the command that sets this. Engaging a pair was observed to force the SECOND (higher-numbered) channel's input_mode and/or gain to match the first -- see channel_link.side_effects.

buses.addressing: Output buses (monitor/headphone) are addressed with the SAME byte position as a per-input channel_offset (frame.command.channel_offset), but the value is a bus id, not a physical input index. Bus ids are NOT contiguous with each other or with channel indices -- do not assume bus id N means 'the Nth bus' in UI order.
buses.notes: Ids 3 and 4 were never sent in any capture. state_report.bus_block has room for 6 evenly-spaced bus slots (ids 0-5, base_offset 28 through 28+3*5=43), and monitor_b sits at the LAST slot (id 5) rather than right after monitor_a -- both facts together are consistent with a guess that 3/4 are reserved for a headphone-3/headphone-4 pair this particular unit doesn't have (other Antelope interfaces have more headphone outs), but this is an unconfirmed guess. Don't build anything on ids 3/4 without a capture from hardware/Launcher config that actually exposes them.

input_mode.evidence: capture2, correlated against user action log (mode selector clicks)

gain.evidence: capture2, gain sweeps per mode, ranges match UI drag limits (not a spec sheet -- worth cross-checking)

phantom.constraint: only send when input_mode == mic; Launcher never exposes the control otherwise
phantom.evidence: capture2, never observed outside mic mode

bus_level.applies_to: buses, not input channels -- send the bus id (see 'buses') in frame.command.channel_offset
bus_level.encoding: 0 = -inf (silent) .. 96 (0x60) = 0dB / unity. Same raw 0-96 byte scale used elsewhere in this protocol (matches the resting/max value seen in gain and meter bytes), but this has only been shown to line up at the two ends (0 and 96) -- the shape of the curve in between (linear dB vs a real analog taper) is NOT confirmed.
bus_level.evidence: captures mona/monb/hp1/hp2 (2026-08): physical volume wheel dragged through its full range for buses 0, 5, 1, and 2 respectively; every SET_PARAM(0x47, bus_id, value) command in the log matched the very next state_report.bus_block reading for that bus_id

bus_dim.evidence: same 4 captures, Dim button toggled on then off in isolation for each bus, matches state_report.bus_block status bit 'dim' (0x08) every time

bus_mute.evidence: same 4 captures, Mute button toggled on then off in isolation for each bus, matches status bit 'mute' (0x04)
bus_mute.notes: In the mona capture, status bit 'mute' (0x04) was also seen flipping on by itself once, on the exact frame bus_level (bus 0) first reached 96/0x60 -- with no SET_PARAM(0x48, ...) command anywhere near it in the log. Unexplained; don't assume 'reaching max volume' sets mute without a dedicated isolated retest -- could well be an unrelated coincidence in this one session. See unresolved_state_offsets.

bus_mono.evidence: same 4 captures, Mono button toggled on then off in isolation for each bus, matches status bit 'mono' (0x10)

channel_link.frame: frame.link_command (a distinct shape from every other param in this file -- NOT SET_PARAM)
channel_link.evidence: capture chlink (2026-08): all 6 pairs (index 0-5) toggled on then off in turn; frame.link_command.pair_index_offset and .enabled_offset were read directly off the wire for all 12 commands (6 on, 6 off) and matched the test sequence exactly
channel_link.side_effects: Engaging a pair's link immediately triggered fresh SET_PARAM(input_mode) and/or SET_PARAM(gain) commands for the SECOND (higher-numbered) channel of that pair -- consistent with the device syncing that channel's mode/gain to the first channel's current settings. Seen for pairs 1, 3, 4, 5 (channels ch4/ch8/ch10/ch12); not seen for pairs 0 or 2, most likely because those channels already matched, not because linking behaves differently for them.
channel_link.live_sync_while_linked: CONFIRMED (capture ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test, 2026-08): while a pair is linked, changing gain, phantom, OR phase_invert on either channel is mirrored to the other channel on essentially every command -- gain_base_offset bytes for both channels moved in lockstep through a full ramp (offsets 49 and 50 tracking together, ~8ms apart), and status_base_offset bytes for both channels flipped together for both the phantom bit (0x10) and the phase_invert bit (0x40). This supersedes the older 'gain/mode only' note below: gain, phantom, and phase_invert all live-sync while linked. input_mode does NOT live-sync -- see mode_requires_unlink.
channel_link.mode_requires_unlink: CONFIRMED (same capture, matches user report): input_mode cannot be changed on a linked pair -- the Launcher grays out the control. The captured workflow was unlink -> change input_mode independently per channel (status_base_offset mode bits for ch1 and ch2 changed at separate, unsynced moments, each also resetting that channel's gain to a value appropriate for the new mode's range) -> re-link. Once re-linked, subsequent phase_invert/phantom/gain changes resumed syncing across both channels immediately (no extra step needed for those three). This is expected device behavior, not a bug in the CLI or a broken link.
channel_link.notes: No 'link enabled' bit has been found yet anywhere in the 0x73 state report -- every state_report byte that changed during this capture is already fully explained by the ordinary gain_base_offset/status_base_offset formula (as a side effect, see above), not a dedicated link flag. Whether link status can be READ BACK from the device at all is unknown; the Launcher UI may just track it client-side from what it has sent. Needs a dedicated whole-report diff (link on vs off, nothing else touched) before concluding there's no readback.

adat_gain.applies_to: the 16 ADAT input channels, a separate address space from the 12 physical hybrid inputs
adat_gain.state_report_offset_formula: adat_gain_base_offset (75) + adat_channel_index (0-indexed: ADAT ch1=0 ... ADAT ch16=15)
adat_gain.evidence: capture adat-ch1-2-3-12-link12 (2026-08): gain swept individually on ADAT ch1 (offset 75), ch2 (offset 76), ch3 (offset 77), and ch12 (offset 86) -- each one-byte-per-channel offset matched 75+index exactly, and the observed value range (-6 .. +12, i.e. 0xfa..0x0c) matches the user-reported UI drag limits for ADAT gain exactly. Same layout pattern as the physical-channel gain_base_offset/status_base_offset formula, just a different base and no accompanying status byte (ADAT has no mode/phantom/phase_invert -- gain and link only). param_id CONFIRMED from the same capture's outgoing 0x70/0x13 frames: every SET_PARAM frame during the sweep used param_id=0x5b, with channel_offset (byte 17) = 0x00/0x01/0x02/0x0b for ADAT ch1/ch2/ch3/ch12 respectively -- exactly matching the readback channel-index formula, and value byte 18 sweeping the full -6..+12 range (0xfa..0x0c). Re-confirmed independently in capture ADAT-link1-2-7-8 (2026-08), same param_id=0x5b, same channel_offset formula, on ADAT ch1/ch3/ch13/ch15.
adat_gain.notes: param_id is a genuinely different value from physical-channel gain's 0x50, not a shared id -- as suspected. build_command()/build_raw_command() with param_id 0x5b and channel_offset = adat_channel_index (0-15) is now the confirmed way to set ADAT gain.

adat_channel_link.frame: frame.link_command -- same opcode (0x14)/param_id (0xa2) as physical channel_link, see notes for an important open caveat about this reuse
adat_channel_link.pairing: pair_index = adat_channel_index // 2, same formula as physical channels but applied to the 16-channel ADAT index space (0-15), giving 8 possible pairs (pair_index 0-7) instead of physical's 6 (0-5)
adat_channel_link.evidence: capture adat-ch1-2-3-12-link12 (2026-08): after ADAT ch1 and ch2 were linked, their gain bytes (offsets 75 and 76) tracked together through a full sweep -- same lockstep pattern as physical-channel links. pair_index CONFIRMED from outgoing 0x70/0x14 frames in that capture: pair_index=0x00 sent right before the ch1/ch2 gain-sync behavior began. Independently re-confirmed and extended in capture ADAT-link1-2-7-8 (2026-08): activating link1/link2/link7/link8 in the Launcher sent pair_index=0x00/0x01/0x06/0x07 respectively, each immediately followed by gain-sync behavior on the matching channel pair (ch1&2, ch3&4, ch13&14, ch15&16) -- pair_index = channel_index//2 holds exactly across all 4 pairs, including the two highest (pair_index 6 and 7) which have no physical-channel equivalent. Full round-trip confirmed: all 4 pairs linked then unlinked in the expected order, enabled byte (offset 19) correctly 0x01 then 0x00 for each.
adat_channel_link.notes: IMPORTANT OPEN QUESTION, not yet resolved: this frame is byte-for-byte identical in shape to the physical-channel SET_LINK frame (same magic/opcode/param_id 0x70/0x14/0xa2, same pair_index and enabled offsets, no other non-zero byte found anywhere in either ADAT link frame dumped so far). Physical pairs use pair_index 0-5; ADAT pairs (now confirmed) use 0-7. That means pair_index values 0-5 are used by BOTH physical and ADAT link commands with no visible disambiguating byte in the frame. Every capture obtained so far (adat-ch1-2-3-12-link12, ADAT-link1-2-7-8) only exercised ADAT links -- no physical-channel link has been toggled in the same session to compare directly. Do NOT assume build_link_command(profile, pair_index, enabled) is safe for ADAT until a capture of an actual physical-pair link toggle is dumped and diffed byte-for-byte against these ADAT frames (all bytes, not just offsets 16-19 -- also worth checking USB-level fields like endpoint/interface in case the disambiguation happens below the HID report itself). Also unconfirmed: the momentary missed-sync bug observed in ADAT-link1-2-7-8 (ch1 dropped to -6 while ch2's mirrored SET_PARAM never arrived, staying at -4) -- a one-off dropped/missed sync frame on the wire, not investigated further per user instruction, but worth another look if it recurs.

master_volume.notes: Not a distinct param -- this IS monitor_a's bus_level (id 0x47, bus 0). Use bus_level/set-bus-level with bus 0 (or 'monitor_a'/'mona'). Kept as a stub entry so 'master volume' still resolves to something if searched for.

routing.notes: Routing matrices are usually multi-cell (source x destination), so this may not fit the single param_id/channel/value shape at all -- could be a different opcode, or channel_offset repurposed as a matrix cell index, or a larger multi-byte payload. Do not assume the existing frame shape applies; confirm from a real capture first. (The discovery of frame.link_command as a genuinely different shape from SET_PARAM is a good reminder that a new feature does not have to reuse the existing frame -- routing may well need its own frame block too.)

unresolved_state_offsets.notes: vumeter-test-ch1 session (2026-08): frame 13306->13310, isolated single-byte change 0x08->0x00, nothing else in the report moved. Unexplained -- not gain/status/mode. RECURS at nearly the same relative time (t~3.05s from start of capture) in TWO more, otherwise-unrelated captures: ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test (frame 13518, t=3.037s) and adat-ch1-2-3-12-link12 (frame 13360, t=3.055s). Neither of those captures had a link/unlink action anywhere near that timestamp (the actual link toggles in ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test happen much later, at t~23s and t~27.6s) -- this rules out the earlier 'possible link-state readback' guess and now favors a periodic/init event that fires ~3s after the capture (or the device connection) starts, independent of user action. Still not deliberately isolated/reproduced on purpose, so keep as unconfirmed, but the 'link readback' hypothesis specifically is now disfavored.

vumeter-test-ch1 session (2026-08): frame 13290->13294, isolated single-byte change 0x06->0x00, nothing else in the report moved, ~16ms before the offset-17 change above (frame 13306). RECURS alongside offset 17 in the same two later captures (ch-link-gain-ph-inv-test frame 13506 t=3.013s; adat-ch1-2-3-12-link12 frame 13336 t=3.007s), same ~3s-from-capture-start timing. See offset-17 note -- same 'periodic/init event around t~3s' hypothesis, same caveat that it's not yet deliberately isolated.

changed during capture, no corresponding test-matrix action. vumeter-test-ch1 session (2026-08): both bytes moved together (0x1f->0x20->0x21->0x60) but only within the first ~0.12s of the capture, before any deliberate user action -- looks like device startup/init behavior rather than something the Launcher UI triggers. Seen again at the start of every one of the mona/monb/hp1/hp2/chlink captures (2026-08), always in that same first fraction of a second, which supports 'startup behavior' over anything test-specific. Not yet deliberately tested.

candidate: per-channel meter/level data embedded directly in the state report (not just the separate 0x75 meter report). vumeter-test-ch1 session (2026-08): offsets 157/169/221 (spacing doesn't match the 1-byte-per-channel gain/status layout -- pattern not yet understood) track together and dropped from their ~0x60 (96) resting value down into the teens/single digits during the loud (mic, gain-75) stretch of the capture, then returned to ~0x60 once gain came back down -- same 'quiet=high, loud=low' shape as the confirmed meter_report.channel_meter_base_offset candidate. The whole 157-176 and 221-232 ranges flicker constantly between 0x5a (90) and 0x60 (96) even at rest, consistent with meter jitter rather than a static setting. Still not a controlled single-variable test -- do a dedicated one-channel sweep (silence/moderate/loud/clip) before trusting the exact byte-to-channel mapping or flipping this to confirmed. Also flickers the same way in the mona/monb/hp1/hp2/chlink captures (2026-08), unrelated to whatever bus/link action was being tested -- further support that this is free-running meter jitter, not a setting.

see 157-176 above -- same session, same evidence, treated as one candidate meter block spanning both ranges rather than two separate features (was previously listed as a separate 'low-cut filter, digital trim, headphone level' guess; that guess is now superseded by the meter-correlation evidence, but not yet disproven).

see params.bus_mute.notes -- status bit 'mute' on bus 0 flipped on, unexplained, in the mona capture (2026-08) at the exact moment bus_level hit its max value (96/0x60), with no SET_PARAM(0x48,...) in the log at that time. Only seen once; not reproduced deliberately. Needs a dedicated retest (ramp a bus to max repeatedly, watch for the mute bit) before treating it as real device behavior rather than a one-off coincidence.

see params.channel_link.notes -- no bit found yet in the 0x73 state report that reflects link on/off state directly; everything observed changing during the chlink capture is explained as a side effect (gain/mode sync onto the second channel of a pair). Needs a dedicated whole-report diff to confirm there really is no readback, rather than it just not having been found.

unresolved_state_offsets.offset: screen brightness / surround EQ pre-post toggle
unresolved_state_offsets.notes: capture settings-scrbrght-surroundEQ (2026-08): dragging the screen-brightness slider through its range and toggling the surround-EQ pre/post switch produced ZERO offset changes anywhere in the 0x73 state report beyond the usual startup ramp (offsets 139/140) and ordinary meter jitter (157-232 block) -- every one of the 272 transitions in that capture is already explained by existing entries. Either these two controls are (a) not reflected in the 0x73 report at all (could live in a different report type/magic, or be host-side-only/not persisted to the device), or (b) the controls genuinely weren't changed during the capture window. Before concluding (a), re-capture with tshark -x confirmed to be logging ALL magics (not just 0x73), and deliberately move each control to its extremes with nothing else touched, to rule out (b) and see if a different magic byte carries this data.
